revised_claim_text: [ASSUMED-N]: Approximately 70% of commercial fleet managers do not share telematics data with their insurer, and roughly 79% report never having been asked — figures sourced exclusively from SambaSafety's self-commissioned 2025 Telematics Report (n=152 fleets); directional gap between telematics adoption and insurer integration is widely acknowledged in trade press but no independent industry-association or audited research-firm survey corroborates the specific percentages. To validate: seek ATRI 'Capitalizing on Telematics' study results (survey launched 2025, results pending), NPTC 2025 Benchmarking Report (member-gated), or commission independent broker survey.
notes: Exhaustive search across ATRI, NPTC, TCA, AM Best, Frost & Sullivan, Carrier Management, and Insurance Journal found no independent corroboration of the 70%/79% figures. ATRI launched a relevant telematics survey in 2025 but results had not been published as of the research date. The NPTC 2025 Benchmarking Report exists but is member-login gated with no publicly extractable insurance data-sharing statistics. The Carrier Management trade article (Nov 2025) re-cites the same SambaSafety source and adds no independent evidence. The Insurance Journal/National Alliance study (Oct 2023) was co-produced with SambaSafety and covers insurer-side UBI readiness, not fleet-to-insurer data sharing rates. SambaSafety's own survey methodology (152 fleets, 180 brokers, 70 carriers, fielded June-July 2025) is disclosed in aggregate but no third-party firm conducted or audited the survey. The directional claim — that most fleets do not share telematics data with insurers — is consistent across SambaSafety's annual reports and acknowledged in trade press, but the specific 70%/79% numbers cannot be upgraded beyond L without an independent source. Score remains L. Recommended action: mark [ASSUMED-N] and flag for validation against ATRI results when published.
